[[Category:Entities]]

######## Masked/ru
{{topicon Fandom}}
{{interlangbox}}
{{Infobox entity|id=MaskedPlayerEnemy
| name = Одержимый
| altname = Маска, Мимик
| power_level = 1
| diversity_level = 0
| max_spawned = 10
| pip_size = Игрок
| door_speed_multiplier = 2
| hits-to-kill = {{#invoke:Entities/AutoHitsToKill|for|MaskedPlayerEnemy}}
| stun_multiplier = 0.75
| attack_damage = Instant kill
| cause_of_death = Strangulation
}}
{{about|the enemy|the scrap item|Masks (Item)}}
'''Одержимый''', также называемый '''Маской''' или '''Мимиком''' - враждебная [[Entities/ru|сущность]] внутри здания. Хотя и имеет способность появляться естественным путём, может также появиться из сотрудника, к которому прилипла [[Masks (Item)|маска]], сделавшая его одержимым. В активном состоянии может свободно входить и выходить из здания, а также стараются вести себя естественно и имитировать поведение обычных сотрудников, дабы приблизиться к ним и схватить для последующего превращения в ещё одного Одержимого. [[Moons/ru|Луна]], на которой он появляется чаще всего - [[Artifice/ru|Artifice]].

Одержимые выглядят, как обычные сотрудники в оранжевой униформе, но с белой маской-комедией сросшейся с их лицом. Их глаза горят ярко-розовым во время процесса превращения другого сотрудника в себе подобного.

<span id="Bestiary_Entry"></span>
== Запись в Бестиарии ==

Не могут быть просканированы.

<span id="Spawn_chances"></span>
== Шансы спавна ==
{{WikiAutomated/EntitySpawnChances|MaskedPlayerEnemy}}
<span id="Mechanics"></span>
== Механики ==

Одержимые появляются двумя способами. Первый - в качестве естественно появившегося противника (будут показываться на радаре синей точкой, как игроки, но переключиться на них будет нельзя), а второй - сотрудник, использовавший [[Masks (Item)|Маску]] или обращённый Одержимым. Маски (предметы) имеют шанс 65% каждые 5 секунд убить сотрудника, держащего её у лица, и превратить его в Одержимого; в инвентаре они безвредны. Если Одержимый появится таким способом, на радаре он будет всё ещё выглядеть, как сотрудник, на него даже можно будет переключиться и наблюдать через корабельные [[Ship/ru#Основной монитор|камеры]] и даже телепортировать его. Сотрудник, который умер от прикладывания к лицу маски-трагедии произведёт Одержимого с маской-трагедией на лице; абсолютно все остальные Одержимые в игре будут с маской-комедией на лице.<ref name="tragedymasked" />

Одержимые, появившиеся естественным путём, всегда будут одеты в оранжевый костюм. Сотрудники, превращённые в Одержимого, будут одеты в [[suits|костюм]], который они носили при жизни.

Одержимые могут слышать звуки. Как только это произойдёт, они посмотрят в сторону источника звука, но могут не всегда двигаться в его сторону чтобы проведать. <ref name=mimic_hear_noise><code>DetectNoise</code> - https://pastebin.com/hKviAUFy</ref>

Одержимые могут пользоваться лифтом в [[Шахты|шахтах]].

Если Одержимый подходит достаточно близко к сотруднику для атаки, он хватает его и извергает в лицо жертвы кровь, превращая её в очередного Одержимого. Одержимый, появившийся из обращённого игрока, сохранит вид сотрудника. Эту атаку можно прервать, если другой сотрудник нанесёт урон атакующему Одержимому.

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
Вопреки популярному мнению, нет никаких сведений о том, что Маска (предмет) пожет присоединиться к лицу игрока после его смерти по другим причинам. Тем не менее, сотрудник, убитый в момент, когда он держал у лица маску, будет иметь маску на своём теле, но если маска прицепилась к лицу сотрудника и затем сотрудника убили, то маска останется прикреплённой к лицу игрока с красными глазами и игрок будет выглядеть, как мёртвый одержимый. Стоит заметить, что такой сценарий не ведёт к одержимости мёртвого тела, так как такое технически невозможно. <ref name="huantedmaskitem_event_loop" />
</div>

Одержимые работают в 3 разных режимах, которые определяют большую часть их повадок:

<span id="Roaming"></span>
=== Блуждание ===

В этом состоянии Одержимые блуждают по карте в поисках сотрудников и их легко определить на радаре, так как они случайным образом осматриваются, часто крутясь по кругу. Одержимые также будут начинать и прекращать бег случайным образом. Это случайное оглядывание и бег завязаны на шкале стамины и управляются логикой, описанной ниже. <ref name="look_and_run_randomly_masked" />

'''Случайное оглядывание'''
 Каждые 0.7-5 секунд:
 Сменить направление налево или направо до 60 градусов за раз.
 Смена занимает от 0.25 до 2 секунд.

'''Случайное начало бега''':
 ЕСЛИ не бегает:
  ЕСЛИ есть хотя бы 5 секунд стамины:
   ЕСЛИ снаружи: шанс начать бег = 35%
   НЕ снаружи: шанс начать бег - 20%

'''Случайное прекращение бега''':
 ЕСЛИ бегает:
  ЕСЛИ стамина = 0: Перестать бежать немедленно
  ИНАЧЕ:
   ЕСЛИ снаружи: шанс прекратить бег = 20%
   НЕ снаружи: шанс прекратить бег = 70%

 -- Если Одержимый прекращает бегать, его шкала стамины устанавливается в значение -6, означая, что он не сможет *случайно* начать бег следующие 11 секунд.

Если во время блуждания в здании нет сотрудников, Одержимый стабильно будет прекращать поиски и направится к выходу.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

Во время блуждания Одержимый будет проверять свою линию видимости на наличие сотрудников. Если сотрудник был замечен, Одержимый перейдёт в стадию преследования.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

Также Одержимые будут наращивать 'интерес' к кораблю в этом состоянии. Когда было набрано достаточно интереса, они перейдёт в состояние засады, если корабль не слишком далеко.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

<span id="Pursuit"></span>
=== Преследование ===

Если Одержимый заметил сотрудника (или её заметили в состоянии Засады), то он переходит в состояние преследования. Когда Одержимый впервые переходит в это состояние, он останавливается и таращится на сотрудника от 2 до 5 секунд<ref name="masked_update" />. Этот таймер немедленно заканчивается, если Одержимому нанесён урон<ref name="masked_hit_enemy" />.

В состоянии преследования он сохраняет зрительный контакт с целью и направляется в её сторону, а логика случайного бега теперь немного отличается от той, что используется в состоянии блуждания. Когда маска преследует цель, процентный шанс и для начала, и для прекращения бега значительно меняются.<ref name="look_and_run_randomly_masked" />

'''Случайное начало бега''':
 ЕСЛИ не бегает:
  ЕСЛИ есть как минимум 5 секунд стамины:
   ЕСЛИ снаружи: шанс начать бег = 11.66%
   НЕ снаружи: шанс начать бег = 6.66%

'''Случайное прекращение бега''':
 ЕСЛИ уже бегает:
  ЕСЛИ стамина = 0: Перестать бежать немедленно
  ИНАЧЕ:
   ЕСЛИ снаружи: шанс прекратить бег = 84%
   НЕ снаружи: шанс прекратить бег = 94%

Далее, если дистанция до их цели больше 17 единиц, они гарантированно начнут бежать, прекращая только по достижении дистанции в 12 единиц до цели или если у них закончится стамина.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

Одержимые перестанут таращиться и преследовать цель, если линия видимости была прервана как минимум на 3.5 секунды. По истечению этого времени сочтут цель 'потерянной в погоне' и начнут искать её, ходя рядом. После истечения 10 секунд с момента прерывания линии видимости они вернутся в состояние блуждания.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

Интересно, что Одержимые расширяют, но укорачивают свой угол обзора в этом состоянии по сравнению с таковым в состоянии блуждания. Он меняется с угла в 45 градусов и дальности в 60 единиц на угол в 70 градусов и дальность в 50 единиц. Дополнительно, Одержимые обладают 'осознанием ближайшего окружения', что значит, что они могут 'видеть' вокруг себя на 1 единицу дальности.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

Одержимые могут сменить цель в этом состоянии, если другой сотрудник в их поле зрения находится ближе<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />.

<span id="Ambush"></span>
=== Засада ===

Одержимые переходят в состояние засады, если у них накопилось достаточно 'интереса' за время блуждания по зданию. В этом состоянии они начинают двигаться к кораблю и ищут место внутри, в котором можно спрятаться. <ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

Во время движения к кораблю Одержимые будут терять к нему интерес, в конце-концов возвращаясь в состояние блуждания<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />. Если Одержимый забрался в корабль, он уже не потеряет к нему интерес, оставаясь в этом состоянии пока не увидит сотрудника или не будет сам замечен сотрудником<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />. В ожидании в засаде Одержимые пригнутся. Примечательно, это единственная ситуация, когда Одержимые вообще приседают.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

В этом состоянии Одержимые снова изменят свой угол обзора. Переходя от угла в 45 градусов и дальности в 60 единиц к углу в 70 градусов и дальности в 20 единиц по сравнению с углом обзора в состоянии блуждания.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

<span id="Strategy"></span>
== Стратегия ==

При виде Одержимого рекомендуется набрать как можно больше дистанции и открытого пространства между ним и собой, а также убедиться, что все сотрудники знают о его присутствии чтобы избежать появления ещё большего количества Одержимых.

Одержимые не сохраняют на себе [[Spray paint/ru|Спрей-краску]], делая возможным определить по отсутствию этого признака одержимость.

Если сотрудник обращается в Одержимого, анимация обращения достаточно длинная, чтобы другие сотрудники при хорошей скорости реакции и координации могли убить случайно появившегося Одержимого или хотя бы навредить Одержимому, который появится из обращённого сотрудника.

Подобно хватке [[Forest Keeper/ru|Хранителя Леса]], есть маленькое окно времени, когда сотрудник может быть спасён союзниками (особенно если присутствует несколько сотрудников) ударом по Одержимому холодным оружием и его убийством, успешным телепортом или оглушением [[Stun Grenade/ru|светошумовой гранатой]], [[Homemade Flashbang|самодельной светошумовой гранатой]], [[Zap Gun/ru|электро-пушкой]] или [[Radar-booster/ru|радарным усилителем]].

[[Shovel/ru|Лопатой]] можно избавиться от Одержимого с относительной лёгкостью, так как дальность удара лопаты больше, чем дальность захвата Одержимым. Использование для убийства [[kitchen knife|кухонного ножа]] возможно, но из-за значительно меньшей дальности удара это намного рискованнее.

На мониторе Одержимые всё ещё будут выглядеть, как сотрудники и визуальных различий между ними нет за исключением их поведения. Во время блуждания маски будут часто вращаться покругу, при этом направление движения не будет изменяться на основе направления взгляда. сотрудники, превращённые в Одержимых будут видны, как обычные сотрудники, несмотря на одержимое поведение сотрудника, и могут быть телепортированы, неся угрозу остальным сотрудникам на корабле. На Одержимых, не являвшимися сотрудниками (то есть появившимися "натурально" во время дня) нельзя переключиться на мониторе, давая подсказку о том, где находится Одержимый.

[[Inverse teleporter|Инверсный телепорт]] не способен убрать Одержимого с корабля.

Одержимые похоже также способны на осуществление простых стратегий, так, группы из 2 или 3 будут координироваться, чтобы завести сотрудников в ловушку. Это наиболее заметно рядом с кораблём, так как обычно один Одержимый спрячется внутри корабля, пока остальные патрулируют территорию возле корабля.

Одержимых могут атаковать [[Eyeless dog/ru|Слепые Псы]] при столкновении, но целенаправленно безглазые псы Одержимых не атакуют. [[Old Bird/ru|Старые Птицы]] атакуют всех сущностей в поле зрения, включая Одержимых. При продолжительном нахождении в близости, Одержимых могут атаковать [[Baboon hawk/ru|Бабуиновые Ястребы]], но это происходит нечасто, даже на [[Adamance/ru|Adamance]].

<span id="Trivia"></span>
== Интересные факты ==
* Одержимые, вопреки популярному мнению, '''НЕ''' вдохновлены SCP-035, что было сказано в статье на патреоне.
* сотрудники, убитые Одержимым, не роняют свои предметы или лут.
* Существует такая вещь, как "масочная рулетка", где все сотрудники поочереди надевают маску, и того, кто станет Одержимым, убивают, тем самым делаю игру опасно весёлой.
* И живые, и мёртвые Одержимый издают смех подобно предмету маска-комедия.

=== [[Version 49|Версия 49]] ===
Неизвестный хотфикс.

=== [[Version 47|Версия 47]] ===
Исправлена ошибка, происходившая, когда процесс обращения сотрудника Одержимым прерывался, что приводило либо к тому, что сотрудник застревал, либо к тому, что он не мог поворачивать мышкой и синхронизировать свои перемещения с другими сторудниками.

Предотвращён случай, когда Одержимый мог создавать дюжины дубликатов одного и того же сотрудника, если каким-то образом этот сотрудник не мог умереть, приводя к хаосу.

######## Masked/zh-cn
{{topicon Fandom}}
{{interlangbox}}
{{Infobox entity|id=MaskedPlayerEnemy
| name = 覆面者
| altname = 面具人、假人
| power_level = 1
| diversity_level = 0
| max_spawned = 10
| pip_size = 玩家
| door_speed_multiplier = 2
| hits-to-kill = {{#invoke:Entities/AutoHitsToKill|for|MaskedPlayerEnemy}}
| stun_multiplier = 0.75
| attack_damage = Instant kill
| cause_of_death = Strangulation
}}
{{about|the enemy|the scrap item|Masks (Item)}}
<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
这种实体被称为“覆面者”，不过通常称为“假人”或“面具人”，整体外观与普通玩家无异。除了它们脸上戴着[[Masks (Item)|悲剧/喜剧面具]]与固定穿着橙色制服之外，很难从视觉上将它们与正常员工区分开来。覆面者会在设施的可通行区域内游荡，其主要目标是追捕它遇到的所有玩家。覆面者可以蹲下，但它们只会在飞船内躲藏并埋伏玩家时蹲下。
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked appear as typical employees with orange uniforms, though with a white comedy mask fused to their heads. Their eyes glow a bright pink while they are in the process of infecting employees.
</div>

<span id="Bestiary_Entry"></span>
== 生物条目 ==

目前无法被扫描。

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
== Spawn chances ==
</div>
{{WikiAutomated/EntitySpawnChances|MaskedPlayerEnemy}}
<span id="Mechanics"></span>
== 机制 ==

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
目前，覆面者有两种生成方式。
* 自然生成。以这种方式生成的覆面者会在[[Ship|监视器]]上显示为类似玩家的小蓝点，但无法将监视目标切换至其或将其传送至飞船内；
* 玩家手持[[Masks (Item)|任意面具]]时，面具每 5 秒有 65% 的概率附身并杀死玩家（只放在物品栏中则不会）。以这种方式生成的覆面者仍显示为玩家，可将监视目标切换到它身上，甚至可被传送回飞船。
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Naturally spawned Masked will always wear the default orange suit. Employees converted into Masked who were wearing [[suits]] purchased from the store will retain their original suit.
</div>

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
覆面者'''可以'''检测声音。一旦它听见声音，它会看向声源方向，但不一定会移动过去调查。<ref name="mimic_hear_noise" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked can operate the elevator in the [[Interiors|mineshaft interior]].
</div>

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
如果玩家位于覆面者的攻击范围内，覆面者会抓住玩家并向其脸部喷血，使玩家转变为另一个覆面者。新的覆面者会继承原玩家的属性。
</div>

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
尽管人们认为面具能附身在玩家尸体上，但目前没有迹象可证明这一点。
然而，佩戴面具时被杀的玩家会把面具戴在脸上，此时面具的眼睛会变成红色，看起来就像一个戴着面具的死人。请注意，这种情况不会导致产生尸体，因为这是不可能的。<ref name=“huandemaskitem_event_loop”/>
</div>

覆面者有 3 种行为模式：

<span id="Roaming"></span>
=== 漫游 ===

在此模式下，覆面者会在地图内漫游以搜寻玩家。搜寻过程中，它们会随机地旋转视角（通常表现为转圈），因此很容易从雷达上识别出来，同时它们也会随机地开始或停止奔跑。以上两种行为依赖一个体力条，其行为逻辑如下：<ref name="look_and_run_randomly_masked" />

'''随机改变视角'''：
  每 0.7~5 秒内：
  向左/右改变方向，最多 60 度。
  每次方向改变需 0.25~2 秒。

'''随机开始奔跑'''： 
  如果 未在奔跑：
   如果 体力至少可维持 5 秒钟：
     如果 位于室外：开始奔跑概率 = 35%
     否则：开始奔跑概率 = 20%

'''随机停止奔跑'''：
  如果 正在奔跑：
   如果 体力值 = 0：立即停止奔跑
   否则：
     如果 位于室外：停止奔跑概率 = 20%
     否则：停止奔跑概率 = 70%
 
  -- 如果覆面者停止奔跑，它的体力值将被设为 -6，意味着它将无法在 11 秒内再次*随机地*奔跑。

如果覆面者在设施内漫游时，设施内没有玩家，覆面者将停止搜索并前往出口。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

覆面者会在漫游时检测视线内的所有玩家。如果覆面者看见玩家，它会切换至追逐模式。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

此外，覆面者会在此模式下累计对飞船的“兴趣值”。当覆面者的兴趣值累计地足够多且离飞船不远时，它会切换至埋伏模式。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

<span id="Pursuit"></span>
=== 追逐 ===

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
覆面者在看见员工（或在埋伏模式被员工看见）后就会开始追逐目标员工。覆面者在刚切换至此模式时会停止移动并注视目标员工 2~5 秒<ref name="masked_update" />。若覆面者在此期间受击，计时器会立即归零<ref name="masked_hit_enemy" />。
</div>

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
在追逐模式下，覆面者会保持与目标的视线接触，并开始向目标移动。值得一提的是，追逐模式下覆面者随机开始或停止奔跑的逻辑与漫游模式的逻辑不同，具体表现为触发概率有显著差别。<ref name="look_and_run_randomly_masked" />
</div>

'''随机开始奔跑'''：
  如果 未在奔跑：
   如果 体力至少可维持 5 秒钟：
     如果 位于室外：开始奔跑概率 = 11.66%
     否则：开始奔跑概率 = 6.66%

'''随机停止奔跑'''：
  如果 正在奔跑：
   如果 体力值 = 0：立即停止奔跑
   否则：
     如果 位于室外：停止奔跑概率 = 84%
     否则：停止奔跑概率 = 94%

此外，如果覆面者离目标的寻路路径长度大于 17 个单位，它必定会开始奔跑，并且只会在体力耗尽或离目标小于 12 个单位远时停止奔跑。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

若覆面者与员工的视线中断 3.5 秒及以上，它会停止注视或追逐员工，并认为自己“追丢了”目标。此后，覆面者会在附近漫游以寻找目标。在视线中断 10 秒后，覆面者会切换回漫游模式。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

有趣的是，与漫游模式相比，覆面者会在此模式下同时拓宽和缩小自身的视野范围，具体为由原先的宽 45、范围 60 变为宽 70、范围 50。另外，覆面者会在此模式下获得“近距离感知”能力，这意味着它能“看见”自身周围一圈（1 个单位）的情况。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
此模式还有一点值得注意，覆面者可以随时将自己的目标切换到在它视线内离它更近的玩家身上<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />。
</div>

<span id="Ambush"></span>
=== 埋伏 ===

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
如果覆面者在设施中漫游时积累了足够的“兴趣值”，它就会切换到埋伏模式。在此模式下，它会向飞船移动，随后在飞船内寻找躲藏点并躲藏。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

在向飞船移动时，覆面者对飞船的“兴趣值”会逐渐降低，最终使其切换回漫游状态<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />。如果覆面者已在飞船内，它的“兴趣值”便不会再降低，而是一直保持埋伏模式，直到它看见员工或被员工看见<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />。在埋伏期间，覆面者会蹲下，而这也是它唯一会蹲下的时刻。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

在此模式下，覆面者会再次改变自身的视野范围。与漫游模式相比，覆面者的视野范围由宽 45、范围 60 变为宽 70、范围 20。<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />

<span id="Strategy"></span>
== 策略 ==

如果你发现了覆面者，建议尽可能与之保持最大距离，并保证周围有足够的开阔空间。同时，确保通知其他所有玩家，以免生成更多的覆面者。

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
覆面者不会保留原玩家身上的[[Spray Paint|喷漆痕迹]]，可以此作为辨别依据。
</div>

玩家被覆面者转换的过程动画很长，足以在动画期间击杀覆面者。因此，若反应及时且团队配合良好，你可以杀死任何意外生成的覆面者，并至少对由玩家转变而成的覆面者造成伤害。

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
与[[Forest Keeper/zh-cn|森林守护者]]的抓捕行为类似，有一个短暂的窗口期可让被抓捕的玩家为其他人所救，尤其是多名玩家同时在场的时候。使用近战武器击杀覆面者，或成功地使用传送，亦或使用[[Stun Grenade/zh-cn|震撼弹]]、[[Homemade Flashbang|土制闪光弹]]、[[Zap Gun/zh-cn|电击枪]]或[[Radar Booster/zh-cn|雷达增幅器]]使覆面者眩晕都可解救玩家。
</div>

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
[[Shovel|铲子]]的攻击范围比覆面者的抓捕范围要大，因此它可以相对容易地击杀覆面者。
</div>

在监视器中，覆面者除了在漫游时经常打转这一行为特征外，视觉上与正常玩家并无差异。变成覆面者的玩家将仍被视为正常员工，尽管该玩家有戴面具的行为，但仍然可以被传送，给船上的其他玩家带来危险。非玩家的覆面者（即原生覆面者）在显示器上没有可切换的位置，因此可以提供覆面者位置的信息。

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
The [[inverse teleporter]] cannot remove a Masked from the ship.
</div>

覆面者似乎具备简单的策略能力，因为 2~3 人一组的它们会协同设陷来困住玩家。这在飞船附近尤为明显，通常一个覆面者会躲藏在飞船内，而其它覆面者则在飞船周围区域巡逻。

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
如果覆面者与[[Eyeless Dog/zh-cn|无眼狗]]发生模型接触，无眼狗将会攻击覆面者。但无眼狗并不会主动攻击覆面者。
</div>

<span id="Trivia"></span>
== 杂项 ==
* 与普遍认知相反，Patreon 上的一条帖子声明了覆面者的灵感'''并非'''来源于 [https://scp-wiki-cn.wikidot.com/scp-035 SCP-035]。
* 若玩家被覆面者杀死，其身上的物品不会掉在地上。
* 有一种叫做“面具轮盘”的游戏，所有员工轮流戴上面具，而成功戴上面具的人会被杀死，因此游戏变得非常有趣。
<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
* Both living and dead Masked can make the same laughing noises as the comedy mask item.
</div>

== 历史 ==

######## Masked/zh-hans
{{topicon Fandom}}
{{interlangbox}}

{{about|the enemy|the scrap item|Masks (Item)}}
<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">
== 概览 ==
这种实体被称为“覆面者”，不过通常称为“伪人”或“面具人”，整体外观与普通玩家无异。除了它们脸上戴着[[Masks (Item)|悲剧/喜剧面具]]之外，很难从视觉上将它们与正常员工区分开来。覆面者会在设施中游荡，其主要目标是追捕它遇到的所有玩家。
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked appear as typical employees with orange uniforms, though with a white comedy mask fused to their heads. Their eyes glow a bright pink while they are in the process of infecting employees.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">

</div>

<div class="mw-translate-fuzzy">

</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
== Spawn chances ==
</div>
{{WikiAutomated/EntitySpawnChances|MaskedPlayerEnemy}}
<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
== Mechanics ==
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked spawn two ways. The first is naturally as an enemy (these will still show up as a blue dot like an employee, but cannot be switched to and teleported on the cameras), while the other is by an employee using a [[Masks (Item)|Mask]]. Tragedy masks and Comedy masks have a 65% chance every 5 seconds to possess and kill the employee holding it up to their face; they are otherwise harmless. If a Masked is spawned this way, it still appears as an employee on [[Ship|cameras]] and can even be teleported. An employee who is killed by putting on a Tragedy mask will produce a Masked with a tragedy mask; all other Masked will have comedy masks.<ref name="tragedymasked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Naturally spawned Masked will always wear the default orange suit. Employees converted into Masked who were wearing [[suits]] purchased from the store will retain their original suit.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked can detect sound. Upon hearing a sound, they look towards it but may not always move towards the sound's source to investigate.<ref name="mimic_hear_noise" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked can operate the elevator in the [[Interiors|mineshaft interior]].
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
If the Masked gets in range to attack an employee, it grabs them and vomits blood into their face, converting them into another Masked. This will spawn them with employee properties. This attack can be interrupted if another employee hits the Masked with a [[shovel]].
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Despite popular belief, there is no indication that a mask can attach to an employee's body postmortem. An employee killed while holding the mask up to their face will drop it near their body, but if the mask attaches to an employee's face and the employee is killed by other means in the short interval before the mask itself kills them, the employee will have the mask attached to their face with red eyes, and will appear as a dead masked. Note that this scenario does not lead to possession of a dead body, as that is not possible. <ref name="huantedmaskitem_event_loop" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked operate in 3 different modes which determine the majority of their behavior:
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
=== Roaming ===
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
In this state, Masked roam around the map searching for employees and are most easily distinguished on the radar as they look around randomly, often spinning in circles. Masked will also start and stop running based on random chance. This random looking and running adheres to a stamina bar and is governed by the logic described underneath. <ref name="look_and_run_randomly_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
'''Randomly looking''': 
  Every 0.7 to 5 seconds:
  Change direction left or right up to 60 degrees at a time.
  Taking 0.25 to 2 seconds to change.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
'''Randomly start running''': 
  IF not running:
    IF has at least 5 seconds of stamina:
      IF outside: chance to start running = 35%
      NOT outside: chance to start running = 20%
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
'''Randomly stop running''':
  IF already running:
    IF stamina = 0: Stop running immediately
    ELSE:
      IF outside: chance to stop running = 20%
      NOT outside: chance to stop running = 70%
 
  -- If a Masked stops running it will set its stamina bar to -6, meaning it is unable to run *randomly* for 11 seconds.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
If no employees are inside the facility whilst in the roaming state, a mask will consistently stop its search and head for the exit.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
While roaming, Masked will check their line of sight for any employee. If an employee is seen, it will switch to the Pursuit state.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Furthermore, Masked will build up 'interest' in the ship whilst in this state. When enough interest is gathered, they will switch to the Ambush state if the ship is not too far away from their position.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
=== Pursuit ===
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
In pursuit mode, the Masked has spotted an employee (or the Masked has been seen in ambush mode) and is pursuing them. When the Masked first enters this state, it stops and stares at the targeted employee for 2 to 5 seconds<ref name="masked_update" />. This timer immediately ends if the Masked is damaged<ref name="masked_hit_enemy" />.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
In pursuit mode, it retains eye contact with its target and starts heading towards them. Notably, the running randomly logic differs from the logic in the roaming state. When a Masked is in pursuit, the percentage chance to both stop and start running randomly change significantly.<ref name="look_and_run_randomly_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
'''Randomly start running''': 
  IF not running:
    IF has at least 5 seconds of stamina:
      IF outside: chance to start running = 11.66%
      NOT outside: chance to start running = 6.66%
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
'''Randomly stop running''': 
  IF already running:
    IF stamina = 0: Stop running immediately
    ELSE:
      IF outside: chance to stop running = 84%
      NOT outside: chance to stop running = 94%
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Furthermore, if the route to their target is more than 17 units away, they are guaranteed to start running, only stopping when within 12 units of their target or out of stamina.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked will stop staring at and moving towards an employee if line-of-sight has been broken for at least 3.5 seconds. After this time, Masked will consider their target 'lost in chase', and will start looking for them by walking around. After line-of-sight has been broken for 10 seconds, they revert back to their roaming state.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Interestingly, Masked broaden but also shorten their field-of-view when in this mode compared to the field-of-view in the roaming state. Going from a width of 45 and a range of 60 to a width of 70 and a range of 50. Additionally, Masked gain 'proximity awareness' meaning they can 'see' in a circle (of 1 unit) around them.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked are able to switch their target at any time in this state if another employee is closer in their line-of-sight<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
=== Ambush ===
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked switch to ambush mode if enough 'interest' has been gathered by roaming the facility. When they are in this state, they start walking towards the ship and look for a spot inside the ship to hide in. <ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Whilst moving towards the ship, Masked will lose interest in the ship, eventually returning to a roaming state<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />. If a mask is inside the ship, they will no longer lose interest in the ship, staying in this state until seeing an employee or being seen by an employee<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />. Whilst waiting in ambush, Masked will crouch. Notably, this is the only time Masked ever crouch.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
In this state, Masked change their field of view once again. Going from a width of 45 and a range of 60 to a width of 70 and a range of 20 if compared to their field of view while roaming.<ref name="do_ai_interval_masked" />
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
== Strategy ==
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
It is recommended if you see a Masked to create as much distance and open space as possible, along with making sure all employees know of its existence to not cause more Masked to spawn.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked do not retain any [[Spray paint]] on them, allowing possible indication of possession.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
If an employee is transforming into a Masked, the animation of the possession is long enough for another employee to kill the Masked. Because of this, with good reaction time and teamwork you can kill any accidental spawns, and at least damage Masked formed from employees turning.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Similar to the [[Forest Keeper|forest keeper]]'s grab, there is a small window to where the employee may be saved by another party especially if multiple employees are present. Hitting the Masked with a melee weapon and killing it, a successful teleport, or stunning it with a [[Stun grenade]], [[Homemade flashbang]], [[Zap gun]], or a [[Radar-booster]].
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
A [[Shovel|shovel]] can dispatch a Masked with relative ease as a shovel has more range than a Masked's grab. Using a [[kitchen knife]] is possible but much riskier due to its short range.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
On the monitor, Masked will still seem like employees and there is no visual difference except in their behavior. Masked will frequently spin in circles when roaming. Employees turned into Masked will be seen as normal employees, despite the Masked behavior of the employee and can still be teleported, bringing danger to other employees on the ship. Masked that are not employees (i.e. spawned Masked) will not have a switchable spot on the monitor, therefore giving clues as to where a Masked is.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
The [[inverse teleporter]] cannot remove a Masked from the ship.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked also seem to be capable of simple strategy, as groups of 2 or 3 will coordinate to trap employees. This is most evident when by the ship as one masked will usually hide inside while the others patrol the area around the ship.
</div>

<div lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr">
Masked can be hurt by [[eyeless dog]]s when coming into contact with them, but eyeless dogs do not intentionally attack Masked. [[Old Bird]]s target all entities within their field of vision, including Masked. [[Baboon hawk]]s can attack Masked if they remain in proximity for prolonged periods of time, but this is uncommon, even on [[Adamance]].
</div>

== Description ==
The Tragedy and Comedy '''Masks''' are scrap items resembling plastic or ceramic theatre masks. For 10 seconds after a mask is initially picked up, it will not be able to possess a employee. After this, while held up to a employee's face, there is a 65% chance every 5 seconds that the mask will possess the employee. This 65% chance is also rolled every time the player starts wearing it. An employee being possessed will die and turn into a [[Masked]] after a few seconds.

Masks cannot possess an employee if the employee does not put it on themselves. Dying with a mask in one's inventory or holding it without putting it on does nothing.

== Spawn chances ==

Both masks have independent spawn chances, but they spawn on the same [[moons]], with [[Offense]] as the one exception.

<tabber>|-|
Tragedy={{#invoke:Scraps/AutoTables|scrapSpawnChancesTables|TragedyMask}}
|-|
Comedy={{#invoke:Scraps/AutoTables|scrapSpawnChancesTables|ComedyMask}}</tabber>

Masks have a chance of playing a crying or laughing sound, depending whether or not it is a Tragedy or Comedy. [[Eyeless Dogs]] are able to hear these cries/laughs.

== Trivia ==

* The Comedy Mask and the Tragedy Mask are, despite popular belief, not inspired by SCP-035, as stated in a Patreon post. <!-- which one??? cite it-->
* The Masks have a chance to make a sound. Either a laughing or a crying one, depending on the mask type.
* Putting on either of the masks while on [[Gordion]] will result in the employee dying without being converted into a Masked. The Mask and the player's other items will still be lost.
* Employees killed while the mask is infecting them will have a death pose similar to that of an employee, but with a mask on their face with red eyes, instead of black eyes.

<translate>
<!--T:1-->
This article is meant to give experienced employees an in-depth view behind various game mechanics such as [[Entities|entity]] spawning, game cycles, [[Scrap|scrap]] collection and much more to come.

<!--T:2-->
All the values and information referenced here is up-to-date as of [[Version_81|Version 81]].

== Game variables == <!--T:3-->

<!--T:4-->
The infobox on the right provides global variables that define game values. These and other moon / entity / scrap specific variables will be referenced in ''[[w:Camel_case|camel case notation]]'' (e.g. 'Hour Length' will be referred as <code>hourLength</code> and a moon's 'Map Size Multiplier' will be referred as <code>mapSizeMultiplier</code>).

<!--T:5-->
Game variables are static, meaning they are the same for everyone and don't change over the course of a game. They might be adjusted by Zeekerss in future Lethal Company updates.

== General principles == <!--T:6-->

=== Time calculations === <!--T:7-->

<!--T:8-->
Time in Lethal Company is defined by the variables <code>hourLength</code> and <code>hoursCount</code>. To be able to use time with curves, we need to work with ''normalized time''. To get the ''normalized time'', we have to divide current time by the total time (<code>hourLength * hoursCount</code>). Normalized time is a value between 0 and 1 and can be seen as the fraction of the day that has already passed.

=== Animation curves === <!--T:9-->

<!--T:10-->
Many mechanics in Lethal Company are based on Unity's [https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/animeditor-AnimationCurves.html Animation Curves]. An animation curve is a mathematical function, that maps a value X (e.g. Time of Day) to another value Y (e.g. Spawn Chance). In the case of Lethal Company, the curves are interpolated using  [[w:Cubic_Hermite_spline|Hermite cubic spline]] interpolation, which basically means that we are given set of input points, or keyframes (the black dots) and slopes that define how the curve is 'bent' around the points to then calculate the actual curve (the orange line).
Here are the three Entity Spawn Curves of [[Experimentation]].
</translate><br>[[File:Experimentation_spawn_curve.png|x300px]]<br><translate>
<!--T:11-->
And here is the spawn probability curve of a [[Baboon Hawk]].
</translate><br>[[File:Baboon_hawk_probability.png|x300px]]<br><translate>
<!--T:12-->
When describing a value retrieved from a curve, the pseudo-function <code>curve.eval(Y)</code> will be used.

== Entity spawning == <!--T:13-->

<!--T:14-->
Entity spawning in Lethal Company is quite complicated and dependent on a lot of variables. This section provides a very detailed description of the different spawning algorithms and the involved parameters.

<!--T:15-->
The entity spawning cycle runs once for indoor spawns at the start of the round<ref group="note" name="bug" />, then once for every group at the start of each day, and then periodically after that until the day ends or the ship leaves early. The interval of the spawning cycle is dependent on the <code>spawningCooldown</code>. A cooldown of 2 (the default value) means that the game waits for 2 hours before the next spawn cycle is executed.

<!--T:63-->
Spawn waves use a slightly different time calculation than normalized time, referred to henceforth as ''spawn wave time''. Instead of current time, the variable <code>currentHour</code> is used, evaluating to <code>(currentHour * hourLength) / (hourLength * hoursCount)</code>. <code>currentHour</code>, despite its name, is the hour before the next spawn wave, which occurs two hours later. This causes values in the curve to be sampled an hour later than they reasonably should be.<ref group="note" name="bug" />

=== Spawning requirements === <!--T:16-->

<!--T:17-->
The spawning algorithm for an entity category is only executed if that category's '''Power Count''' is not yet at its maximum. For example, if the [[Bracken]] (Power Level 3) and a [[Thumper]] (Power Level 3) are already present on [[Assurance]], the moon's '''Max Indoor Power''' of 6 is reached and no additional indoor entities will spawn until the power count goes down. 

<!--T:18-->
The spawning algorithm for an entity is also limited by the category's '''Diversity Power Count'''. For example, if the [[Feiopar]] (Diversity Power Level 2) and [[Baboon Hawk]] (Diversity Power Level 1) both spawned on [[March]], the moon's '''Max Outdoor Diversity Power''' of 3 is reached. More Feiopars and Baboon Hawks can spawn, but no other entities of a different species will spawn for the whole day. Killing all Feiopars or Baboon Hawks present will not deduct from this counter.

=== Spawning algorithm (Daytime Entities) === <!--T:19-->

<!--T:20-->
The amount of daytime entities spawned is based of the moon's '''Daytime Spawn Probability Curve''' and '''Daytime Spawn Deviation'''. The base spawn count is retrieved from evaluating the curve with the ''spawn wave time''. 

<!--T:21-->
The actual spawn count is a number, randomly chosen in the following range and rounded to the nearest whole number.
*'''Min Spawn Count:''' <code>daytimeCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) - daytimeSpawnDeviation</code>
*'''Max Spawn Count:''' <code>daytimeCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) + daytimeSpawnDeviation</code>

<!--T:22-->
This spawn count is then clamped between 0 and 20. There will never be more than 20 daytime entities on the map at the same time.

<!--T:23-->
After the amount of entities to be spawned has been determined, the game determines which entities to spawn. For each entity slot, a list of spawn probabilities is created based on each entity's eligibility to be spawned. The eligibility is calculated based on the following factors.
*'''Max Count:''' The entity's spawn count wouldn't exceed its own '''Max Count'''
*'''Power Level:''' The added entity's power level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Daytime Power'''
*'''Latest Spawn Time:''' The entity's latest spawn time has not yet passed (e.g. [[Roaming_Locusts|Roaming Locusts]] stop spawning after 7:41 PM)

<!--T:24-->
The spawn chance for ineligible entities is set to 0. Eligible entities get their current moon spawn chance multiplied by their own '''Spawn Probability Curve''' value that is based on the Time of Day. If the entity uses '''Spawn Count Falloff''' and therefore has a '''Spawn Count Falloff''' curve, the spawn chance also gets multiplied by that curve value, evaluated for the amount of already spawned entities of the same type. Finally, the game picks a random weighted index from the list of eligible entities. The selected entity gets spawned immediately at one of the predefined daytime entity spawn points.

=== Spawning algorithm (Outdoor Entities) === <!--T:25-->

<!--T:26-->
The amount of outdoor entities spawned is based of the moon's '''Outdoor Spawn Probability Curve''' and '''Outdoor Spawn Deviation'''. The base spawn count is retrieved from evaluating the curve with the ''spawn wave time''.

<!--T:27-->
The actual spawn count is also a number, randomly chosen from a range and rounded to the nearest whole number. The minimum count is dependent on how many days are left until the quota must be reached (<code>daysUntilDeadline</code>). The more days have passed, the more likely it becomes for entities to spawn.
*'''Min Spawn Count:''' <code>outdoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) + abs(daysUntilDeadline-3) / 1.6 - 3</code>
*'''Max Spawn Count:''' <code>outdoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) + 3</code>

<!--T:28-->
This spawn count is then clamped between <code>minOutsideEnemiesToSpawn</code> and 20. The variable <code>minOutsideEnemiesToSpawn</code> is set to 0 by default but can change to a predefined value if the current moon is [[Weather|eclipsed]]. Each moon has its own <code>minOutsideEnemiesToSpawn</code> during eclipses which can be found on their individual pages. 1 spawn is added to the minimum and maximum if the moon is a challenge moon.

<!--T:29-->
After the amount of entities to be spawned has been determined, the game determines which entities to spawn. For each entity slot, a list of spawn probabilities is created based on each entity's eligibility to be spawned. The eligibility is calculated based on the following factors.
*'''Max Count:''' The entity's spawn count wouldn't exceed its own '''Max Count'''
*'''Power Level:''' The added entity's power level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Outdoor Power'''
*'''Diversity Power Level:''' The added entity's diversity level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Outdoor Diversity Power'''
*'''Latest Spawn Time:''' The entity's latest spawn time has not yet passed

<!--T:30-->
The spawn chance for ineligible entities is set to 0. Eligible entities get their current moon spawn chance multiplied by their own '''Spawn Probability Curve''' value that is evaluated for the current Time of Day. If the entity uses '''Spawn Count Falloff''' and therefore has a '''Spawn Count Falloff''' curve, the spawn chance also gets multiplied by that curve value, evaluated for the amount of already spawned entities of the same type. Finally, the game picks a random weighted index from the list of eligible entities. The selected entity gets spawned immediately at one of the predefined outdoor entity spawn points.

=== Spawning algorithm (Indoor Entities) === <!--T:31-->

<!--T:32-->
The spawn algorithm for indoor entities is more complicated than the previous two, since indoor enemies don't spawn instantly, and are instead assigned a vent and a timer that specifies when the entity will be spawned from that vent.

<!--T:33-->
The amount of indoor entities spawned is based off the moon's '''Indoor Spawn Probability Curve''' and '''Indoor Spawn Deviation'''. The base spawn count is retrieved from evaluating the curve with the ''spawn wave time''.

<!--T:34-->
The actual spawn count is again, a number that is randomly chosen from a range and rounded to the nearest whole number. As with outdoor entities, the minimum count is dependent on how many days are left until the quota must be reached (<code>daysUntilDeadline</code>). The more days have passed, the more likely it becomes for indoor entities to spawn.
*'''Min Spawn Count:''' <code>(indoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) - 1) + abs(daysUntilDeadline-3) / 1.6 - indoorSpawnDeviation</code>
*'''Max Spawn Count:''' <code>(indoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) - 1) + indoorSpawnDeviation</code>

<!--T:35-->
This spawn count is then clamped between <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> and 20 or the amount of free vents on the map. Every selected entity must be able to be assigned to a free vent later. 1 spawn is added to the minimum and maximum if the moon is a challenge moon.

<!--T:64-->
The variable <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> is set to 0 by default but can change to a predefined value if the current moon is [[Weather|eclipsed]], or to 2 (with a 70% chance) when an [[apparatus]] is collected. Each moon has its own <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> during eclipses which can be found on their individual pages.

<!--T:36-->
In addition to this, before clamping occurs, if ''one day has already passed'' and <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> ''is still set to 0'' (the current moon is ''not eclipsed'', and ''apparatus has not increased spawn rates''), <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> will be set to 1 if one of the following conditions is met.
* Percentage of scrap found in the current round is greater than or equal to the profit quota and it's after 11:24 AM (intended to be greater than 80% of quota, but a typo causes percentage to round down to a multiple of 100%)
* Percentage of scrap found in the current round is greater than 65% of the total scrap value on the map
* At least 5 rounds have passed (total, not necessarily consecutively) where more than 30 credits worth of scrap was collected and no players died. If a player dies at any point, the count starts over from 0.

<!--T:37-->
After the amount of entities to be spawned has been determined, the game determines which entities to spawn. For each entity slot, a list of spawn probabilities is created based on each entity's eligibility to be spawned. The eligibility is calculated based on the following factors.
*'''Max Count:''' The entity's spawn count wouldn't exceed its own '''Max Count'''
*'''Power Level:''' The added entity's power level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Indoor Power'''
*'''Diversity Power Level:''' The added entity's diversity level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Indoor Diversity Power'''
*'''Latest Spawn Time:''' The entity's latest spawn time has not yet passed

<!--T:38-->
The spawn chance for ineligible entities is set to 0. Eligible entities get their current moon spawn chance multiplied by their own '''Spawn Probability Curve''' value that is evaluated for the current time of day. Entities that use '''Spawn Count Falloff''' and therefore have a '''Spawn Count Falloff''' curve, also have their spawn chance multiplied by that curve's value, evaluated for the amount of already spawned entities of that same type.

<!--T:39-->
Finally, the game picks a random weighted index from the list of eligible entities. The selected entity is then assigned to a randomly picked free vent on the map alongside a randomly determined ''spawn delay''. The spawn delay is clamped between the current time and the start of the next spawn cycle.

<!--T:40-->
An indoor entity's <code>spawningDelay</code> defines how far in advance the vent crawling sound will be played. The sound starts off quiet and gets louder over time. Once the <code>spawningDelay</code> is over the sound stops, the vent opens and the assigned entity spawns in front of the vent. The vent then resets and is ready to be assigned again in the next spawn cycle.

===Entity Infestations=== <!--T:41-->

<!--T:42-->
At the start of every day, the game rolls a 0.4% chance. If the current date is October 23rd (Lethal Company's anniversary), then it also rolls a ~4.545% chance. If either rolls succeed (~4.927% chance), then the current day may have an indoor infestation.{{ref code|RoundManager.RefreshEnemiesList}}<ref group="note" name="infestation chance" />

<!--T:43-->
There are currently two types of infestations. If [[Nutcracker|Nutcrackers]] are on the list of indoor entities and a 25% roll succeeds, the facility will have a Nutcracker infestation. Otherwise, if [[Hoarding Bug|Hoarding Bugs]] are on the list of indoor entities, the facility will have a Hoarding Bug infestation. If neither conditions are met, the infestation is ignored.{{ref code|RoundManager.RefreshEnemiesList}}

<!--T:44-->
On infestation days, the respective entity is marked as an infestation entity, the indoor power level is increased to either 30 (for Hoarding Bugs) or 20 (for Nutcrackers){{ref code|RoundManager.RefreshEnemiesList}}, and the 2 spawns are added to the wave{{ref code|RoundManager.PlotOutEnemiesForNextHour}}<ref group="note" name="infestation minimum spawns" />. In addition, all standard spawning probabilities (including probabilities of 0) and probability modifiers are ignored, and the probability is set to 100 for the infestation entity and multiplied by 0.075 for every other entity<ref group="note" name="infestation preferred interior" />. Other things that prevent an entity from spawning (such as max spawns) can still prevent an entity from spawning.{{ref code|RoundManager.AssignRandomEnemyToVent}}

<!--T:45-->
As such, until the max spawns of the infestation entity are reached, almost all spawns will consist of that entity, though occasionally, other entities can spawn as well. Afterwards, every other entity will spawn with equal probability until the power level cap is reached.

<!--T:46-->
Infestations only affect indoor spawns.

=== Special Enemies === <!--T:47-->

<!--T:48-->
The '''special enemy system''' is used to prioritize specific enemy spawns on a moon during each spawn wave. After normal spawn weights have been calculated, the special enemy's weight is set to a weight that matches the defined percentage. If the percentage is 100%, every spawn wave is artificially forced to have at least one of this defined enemy, unless it has already reached its maximum count, or the moon's indoor power level has been reached. 

<!--T:49-->
A special enemy does not have to exist for every moon. This system is only currently utilized by the [[Cadaver Growth]]s on [[Adamance]], with a percentage of 100%.

=== Rarity === <!--T:51-->

<!--T:52-->
When spawning in another scrap item, the game uses an <abbr title="(pseudo-)random number generator">RNG</abbr> combined with the 'rarity table' for that particular moon.
These tables are lists of the possible scrap items and their relative rarities, which are simple whole numbers. (You can think of these like "tickets" in a raffle or lottery; having 2 makes it twice as likely to be chosen as having 1.)
<br>Thus, we can calculate the chances of each type of scrap getting spawned as its relative rarity divided by the total of all the rarity values in the table. It's these chances (as percentages) that you'll see in tables like this one across other articles:
</translate>

<!--T:53-->
(The calculations are handled by [[Module:Rarities]], and the datamined rarity tables are stored in subpages of that. See [[Project:WikiAutomated]] for more info.)

== Quota == <!--T:66-->

<!--T:67-->
Quota is increased every four days by a few random factors, the number of quotas passed (<code>quotaCount</code>), and furniture luck. 

<!--T:68-->
An integer value, dubbed the ''quota to add'', is set to <code>(quotaCount * (quotaCount / 16))</code>, increased by 1, then clamped between 0 and 10,000. The randomizer curve value, dubbed the ''curve sample'', is evaluated as a random percentage minus furniture luck * 1.5. Then, the quota to add is multiplied by 100 and <code>randomizerCurve.eval(curveSample) + 1</code>. This is then added to the current quota amount, then clamped between 0 and 1 billion.{{ref code|TimeOfDay.SetNewProfitQuota}}

<!--T:69-->
Overtime credits is decided by subtracting '''total sold - quota''', dividing by 5, and adding or subtracting multiples of 15 dependent on the day sold. On 3 days left, 30 will be added; then 15 added for 2 days, none for 1 day, and 15 subtracted for 0 days. The formula in game is as follows:
* <code>(total sold - quota) / 5 + (15 * daysUntilDeadline)</code>
where <code>daysUntilDeadline</code> is -1 for 0 days left and 2 for 3 days left.

<!--T:70-->
After these values are calculated and set, amount of quota fulfilled is reset, the time until deadline is set to <code>totalTime * 4</code>, present furniture items are added to the luck counter for next quota, and the flag for [[HUD#Advertisements|advertisements]] is reset.

=== Furniture luck === <!--T:71-->

<!--T:72-->
Furniture luck is a system used primarily by quota increase randomization, but is also used to decide [[Vain Shroud]] growth. Each furniture item has a specified luck value, and when the new quota is set, furniture luck is updated to include the percentages of all furniture items that have been present since last quota. Here is the table for each furniture item and its luck:

<!--T:75-->
Furniture must be kept on the ship and unstored for the whole quota for it to factor into luck for the next quota. This is ''not'' the case for items with negative luck, which have a specific case where its luck is always counted if it is ever unstored during the whole quota. This is to prevent exploitation by removing it before the new quota is calculated and negating the negative luck.

<!--T:76-->
For Vain Shroud growth, luck is not recalculated; instead, it is read from the previous quota's luck value, as assigning a new quota is the only time it is recalculated.

This article is meant to give experienced employees an in-depth view behind various game mechanics such as [[Entities|entity]] spawning, game cycles, [[Scrap|scrap]] collection and much more to come.

All the values and information referenced here is up-to-date as of [[Version_81|Version 81]].

== Game variables ==

The infobox on the right provides global variables that define game values. These and other moon / entity / scrap specific variables will be referenced in ''[[w:Camel_case|camel case notation]]'' (e.g. 'Hour Length' will be referred as <code>hourLength</code> and a moon's 'Map Size Multiplier' will be referred as <code>mapSizeMultiplier</code>).

Game variables are static, meaning they are the same for everyone and don't change over the course of a game. They might be adjusted by Zeekerss in future Lethal Company updates.

== General principles ==

=== Time calculations ===

Time in Lethal Company is defined by the variables <code>hourLength</code> and <code>hoursCount</code>. To be able to use time with curves, we need to work with ''normalized time''. To get the ''normalized time'', we have to divide current time by the total time (<code>hourLength * hoursCount</code>). Normalized time is a value between 0 and 1 and can be seen as the fraction of the day that has already passed.

=== Animation curves ===

Many mechanics in Lethal Company are based on Unity's [https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/animeditor-AnimationCurves.html Animation Curves]. An animation curve is a mathematical function, that maps a value X (e.g. Time of Day) to another value Y (e.g. Spawn Chance). In the case of Lethal Company, the curves are interpolated using  [[w:Cubic_Hermite_spline|Hermite cubic spline]] interpolation, which basically means that we are given set of input points, or keyframes (the black dots) and slopes that define how the curve is 'bent' around the points to then calculate the actual curve (the orange line).
Here are the three Entity Spawn Curves of [[Experimentation]].<br>[[File:Experimentation_spawn_curve.png|x300px]]<br>And here is the spawn probability curve of a [[Baboon Hawk]].<br>[[File:Baboon_hawk_probability.png|x300px]]<br>When describing a value retrieved from a curve, the pseudo-function <code>curve.eval(Y)</code> will be used.

== Entity spawning ==

Entity spawning in Lethal Company is quite complicated and dependent on a lot of variables. This section provides a very detailed description of the different spawning algorithms and the involved parameters.

The entity spawning cycle runs once for indoor spawns at the start of the round<ref group="note" name="bug" />, then once for every group at the start of each day, and then periodically after that until the day ends or the ship leaves early. The interval of the spawning cycle is dependent on the <code>spawningCooldown</code>. A cooldown of 2 (the default value) means that the game waits for 2 hours before the next spawn cycle is executed.

Spawn waves use a slightly different time calculation than normalized time, referred to henceforth as ''spawn wave time''. Instead of current time, the variable <code>currentHour</code> is used, evaluating to <code>(currentHour * hourLength) / (hourLength * hoursCount)</code>. <code>currentHour</code>, despite its name, is the hour before the next spawn wave, which occurs two hours later. This causes values in the curve to be sampled an hour later than they reasonably should be.<ref group="note" name="bug" />

=== Spawning requirements ===

The spawning algorithm for an entity category is only executed if that category's '''Power Count''' is not yet at its maximum. For example, if the [[Bracken]] (Power Level 3) and a [[Thumper]] (Power Level 3) are already present on [[Assurance]], the moon's '''Max Indoor Power''' of 6 is reached and no additional indoor entities will spawn until the power count goes down. 

The spawning algorithm for an entity is also limited by the category's '''Diversity Power Count'''. For example, if the [[Feiopar]] (Diversity Power Level 2) and [[Baboon Hawk]] (Diversity Power Level 1) both spawned on [[March]], the moon's '''Max Outdoor Diversity Power''' of 3 is reached. More Feiopars and Baboon Hawks can spawn, but no other entities of a different species will spawn for the whole day. Killing all Feiopars or Baboon Hawks present will not deduct from this counter.

=== Spawning algorithm (Daytime Entities) ===

The amount of daytime entities spawned is based of the moon's '''Daytime Spawn Probability Curve''' and '''Daytime Spawn Deviation'''. The base spawn count is retrieved from evaluating the curve with the ''spawn wave time''. 

The actual spawn count is a number, randomly chosen in the following range and rounded to the nearest whole number.
*'''Min Spawn Count:''' <code>daytimeCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) - daytimeSpawnDeviation</code>
*'''Max Spawn Count:''' <code>daytimeCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) + daytimeSpawnDeviation</code>

This spawn count is then clamped between 0 and 20. There will never be more than 20 daytime entities on the map at the same time.

After the amount of entities to be spawned has been determined, the game determines which entities to spawn. For each entity slot, a list of spawn probabilities is created based on each entity's eligibility to be spawned. The eligibility is calculated based on the following factors.
*'''Max Count:''' The entity's spawn count wouldn't exceed its own '''Max Count'''
*'''Power Level:''' The added entity's power level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Daytime Power'''
*'''Latest Spawn Time:''' The entity's latest spawn time has not yet passed (e.g. [[Roaming_Locusts|Roaming Locusts]] stop spawning after 7:41 PM)

The spawn chance for ineligible entities is set to 0. Eligible entities get their current moon spawn chance multiplied by their own '''Spawn Probability Curve''' value that is based on the Time of Day. If the entity uses '''Spawn Count Falloff''' and therefore has a '''Spawn Count Falloff''' curve, the spawn chance also gets multiplied by that curve value, evaluated for the amount of already spawned entities of the same type. Finally, the game picks a random weighted index from the list of eligible entities. The selected entity gets spawned immediately at one of the predefined daytime entity spawn points.

=== Spawning algorithm (Outdoor Entities) ===

The amount of outdoor entities spawned is based of the moon's '''Outdoor Spawn Probability Curve''' and '''Outdoor Spawn Deviation'''. The base spawn count is retrieved from evaluating the curve with the ''spawn wave time''.

The actual spawn count is also a number, randomly chosen from a range and rounded to the nearest whole number. The minimum count is dependent on how many days are left until the quota must be reached (<code>daysUntilDeadline</code>). The more days have passed, the more likely it becomes for entities to spawn.
*'''Min Spawn Count:''' <code>outdoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) + abs(daysUntilDeadline-3) / 1.6 - 3</code>
*'''Max Spawn Count:''' <code>outdoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) + 3</code>

This spawn count is then clamped between <code>minOutsideEnemiesToSpawn</code> and 20. The variable <code>minOutsideEnemiesToSpawn</code> is set to 0 by default but can change to a predefined value if the current moon is [[Weather|eclipsed]]. Each moon has its own <code>minOutsideEnemiesToSpawn</code> during eclipses which can be found on their individual pages. 1 spawn is added to the minimum and maximum if the moon is a challenge moon.

After the amount of entities to be spawned has been determined, the game determines which entities to spawn. For each entity slot, a list of spawn probabilities is created based on each entity's eligibility to be spawned. The eligibility is calculated based on the following factors.
*'''Max Count:''' The entity's spawn count wouldn't exceed its own '''Max Count'''
*'''Power Level:''' The added entity's power level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Outdoor Power'''
*'''Diversity Power Level:''' The added entity's diversity level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Outdoor Diversity Power'''
*'''Latest Spawn Time:''' The entity's latest spawn time has not yet passed

The spawn chance for ineligible entities is set to 0. Eligible entities get their current moon spawn chance multiplied by their own '''Spawn Probability Curve''' value that is evaluated for the current Time of Day. If the entity uses '''Spawn Count Falloff''' and therefore has a '''Spawn Count Falloff''' curve, the spawn chance also gets multiplied by that curve value, evaluated for the amount of already spawned entities of the same type. Finally, the game picks a random weighted index from the list of eligible entities. The selected entity gets spawned immediately at one of the predefined outdoor entity spawn points.

=== Spawning algorithm (Indoor Entities) ===

The spawn algorithm for indoor entities is more complicated than the previous two, since indoor enemies don't spawn instantly, and are instead assigned a vent and a timer that specifies when the entity will be spawned from that vent.

The amount of indoor entities spawned is based off the moon's '''Indoor Spawn Probability Curve''' and '''Indoor Spawn Deviation'''. The base spawn count is retrieved from evaluating the curve with the ''spawn wave time''.

The actual spawn count is again, a number that is randomly chosen from a range and rounded to the nearest whole number. As with outdoor entities, the minimum count is dependent on how many days are left until the quota must be reached (<code>daysUntilDeadline</code>). The more days have passed, the more likely it becomes for indoor entities to spawn.
*'''Min Spawn Count:''' <code>(indoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) - 1) + abs(daysUntilDeadline-3) / 1.6 - indoorSpawnDeviation</code>
*'''Max Spawn Count:''' <code>(indoorCurve.eval(spawnWaveTime) - 1) + indoorSpawnDeviation</code>

This spawn count is then clamped between <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> and 20 or the amount of free vents on the map. Every selected entity must be able to be assigned to a free vent later. 1 spawn is added to the minimum and maximum if the moon is a challenge moon.

The variable <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> is set to 0 by default but can change to a predefined value if the current moon is [[Weather|eclipsed]], or to 2 (with a 70% chance) when an [[apparatus]] is collected. Each moon has its own <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> during eclipses which can be found on their individual pages.

In addition to this, before clamping occurs, if ''one day has already passed'' and <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> ''is still set to 0'' (the current moon is ''not eclipsed'', and ''apparatus has not increased spawn rates''), <code>minEnemiesToSpawn</code> will be set to 1 if one of the following conditions is met.
* Percentage of scrap found in the current round is greater than or equal to the profit quota and it's after 11:24 AM (intended to be greater than 80% of quota, but a typo causes percentage to round down to a multiple of 100%)
* Percentage of scrap found in the current round is greater than 65% of the total scrap value on the map
* At least 5 rounds have passed (total, not necessarily consecutively) where more than 30 credits worth of scrap was collected and no players died. If a player dies at any point, the count starts over from 0.

After the amount of entities to be spawned has been determined, the game determines which entities to spawn. For each entity slot, a list of spawn probabilities is created based on each entity's eligibility to be spawned. The eligibility is calculated based on the following factors.
*'''Max Count:''' The entity's spawn count wouldn't exceed its own '''Max Count'''
*'''Power Level:''' The added entity's power level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Indoor Power'''
*'''Diversity Power Level:''' The added entity's diversity level wouldn't exceed the moon's '''Max Indoor Diversity Power'''
*'''Latest Spawn Time:''' The entity's latest spawn time has not yet passed

The spawn chance for ineligible entities is set to 0. Eligible entities get their current moon spawn chance multiplied by their own '''Spawn Probability Curve''' value that is evaluated for the current time of day. Entities that use '''Spawn Count Falloff''' and therefore have a '''Spawn Count Falloff''' curve, also have their spawn chance multiplied by that curve's value, evaluated for the amount of already spawned entities of that same type.

Finally, the game picks a random weighted index from the list of eligible entities. The selected entity is then assigned to a randomly picked free vent on the map alongside a randomly determined ''spawn delay''. The spawn delay is clamped between the current time and the start of the next spawn cycle.

An indoor entity's <code>spawningDelay</code> defines how far in advance the vent crawling sound will be played. The sound starts off quiet and gets louder over time. Once the <code>spawningDelay</code> is over the sound stops, the vent opens and the assigned entity spawns in front of the vent. The vent then resets and is ready to be assigned again in the next spawn cycle.

===Entity Infestations===

At the start of every day, the game rolls a 0.4% chance. If the current date is October 23rd (Lethal Company's anniversary), then it also rolls a ~4.545% chance. If either rolls succeed (~4.927% chance), then the current day may have an indoor infestation.{{ref code|RoundManager.RefreshEnemiesList}}<ref group="note" name="infestation chance" />

There are currently two types of infestations. If [[Nutcracker|Nutcrackers]] are on the list of indoor entities and a 25% roll succeeds, the facility will have a Nutcracker infestation. Otherwise, if [[Hoarding Bug|Hoarding Bugs]] are on the list of indoor entities, the facility will have a Hoarding Bug infestation. If neither conditions are met, the infestation is ignored.{{ref code|RoundManager.RefreshEnemiesList}}

On infestation days, the respective entity is marked as an infestation entity, the indoor power level is increased to either 30 (for Hoarding Bugs) or 20 (for Nutcrackers){{ref code|RoundManager.RefreshEnemiesList}}, and the 2 spawns are added to the wave{{ref code|RoundManager.PlotOutEnemiesForNextHour}}<ref group="note" name="infestation minimum spawns" />. In addition, all standard spawning probabilities (including probabilities of 0) and probability modifiers are ignored, and the probability is set to 100 for the infestation entity and multiplied by 0.075 for every other entity<ref group="note" name="infestation preferred interior" />. Other things that prevent an entity from spawning (such as max spawns) can still prevent an entity from spawning.{{ref code|RoundManager.AssignRandomEnemyToVent}}

As such, until the max spawns of the infestation entity are reached, almost all spawns will consist of that entity, though occasionally, other entities can spawn as well. Afterwards, every other entity will spawn with equal probability until the power level cap is reached.

Infestations only affect indoor spawns.

=== Special Enemies ===

The '''special enemy system''' is used to prioritize specific enemy spawns on a moon during each spawn wave. After normal spawn weights have been calculated, the special enemy's weight is set to a weight that matches the defined percentage. If the percentage is 100%, every spawn wave is artificially forced to have at least one of this defined enemy, unless it has already reached its maximum count, or the moon's indoor power level has been reached. 

A special enemy does not have to exist for every moon. This system is only currently utilized by the [[Cadaver Growth]]s on [[Adamance]], with a percentage of 100%.

== Scrap spawning ==

{{for|information on days that spawn only one scrap type|Single scrap day}}

=== Rarity ===

When spawning in another scrap item, the game uses an <abbr title="(pseudo-)random number generator">RNG</abbr> combined with the 'rarity table' for that particular moon.
These tables are lists of the possible scrap items and their relative rarities, which are simple whole numbers. (You can think of these like "tickets" in a raffle or lottery; having 2 makes it twice as likely to be chosen as having 1.)
<br>Thus, we can calculate the chances of each type of scrap getting spawned as its relative rarity divided by the total of all the rarity values in the table. It's these chances (as percentages) that you'll see in tables like this one across other articles:
{{#invoke:Moons/AutoTables|lootTable|Dine}}
(The calculations are handled by [[Module:Rarities]], and the datamined rarity tables are stored in subpages of that. See [[Project:WikiAutomated]] for more info.)

== Quota ==

Quota is increased every four days by a few random factors, the number of quotas passed (<code>quotaCount</code>), and furniture luck. 

An integer value, dubbed the ''quota to add'', is set to <code>(quotaCount * (quotaCount / 16))</code>, increased by 1, then clamped between 0 and 10,000. The randomizer curve value, dubbed the ''curve sample'', is evaluated as a random percentage minus furniture luck * 1.5. Then, the quota to add is multiplied by 100 and <code>randomizerCurve.eval(curveSample) + 1</code>. This is then added to the current quota amount, then clamped between 0 and 1 billion.{{ref code|TimeOfDay.SetNewProfitQuota}}

Overtime credits is decided by subtracting '''total sold - quota''', dividing by 5, and adding or subtracting multiples of 15 dependent on the day sold. On 3 days left, 30 will be added; then 15 added for 2 days, none for 1 day, and 15 subtracted for 0 days. The formula in game is as follows:
* <code>(total sold - quota) / 5 + (15 * daysUntilDeadline)</code>
where <code>daysUntilDeadline</code> is -1 for 0 days left and 2 for 3 days left.

After these values are calculated and set, amount of quota fulfilled is reset, the time until deadline is set to <code>totalTime * 4</code>, present furniture items are added to the luck counter for next quota, and the flag for [[HUD#Advertisements|advertisements]] is reset.

=== Furniture luck ===

Furniture luck is a system used primarily by quota increase randomization, but is also used to decide [[Vain Shroud]] growth. Each furniture item has a specified luck value, and when the new quota is set, furniture luck is updated to include the percentages of all furniture items that have been present since last quota. Here is the table for each furniture item and its luck:

|-
| [[Classic painting]] || 0.60%
|- 
| [[Cozy lights]] || 0.50%
|- 
| [[Disco ball]] || 6.00%
|- 
| [[Dog house]] || 0.70%
|- 
| [[Electric chair]] || 1.20%
|- 
| [[Fridge]] || 1.00%
|- 
| [[Goldfish]] || 0.60%
|- 
| [[Inverse Teleporter]] || 0.40%
|- 
| [[Jack-o-Lantern]] || 1.20%
|- 
| [[Loud horn]] || 0.25%
|- 
| [[Microwave]] || 1.00%
|- 
| [[Plushie pajama man]] || 0.30%
|- 
| [[Record player]] || 0.50%
|- 
| [[Romantic table]] || 0.50%

Furniture must be kept on the ship and unstored for the whole quota for it to factor into luck for the next quota. This is ''not'' the case for items with negative luck, which have a specific case where its luck is always counted if it is ever unstored during the whole quota. This is to prevent exploitation by removing it before the new quota is calculated and negating the negative luck.

For Vain Shroud growth, luck is not recalculated; instead, it is read from the previous quota's luck value, as assigning a new quota is the only time it is recalculated.
